how_these_were_written: Phrasings an operator types when they come back to a project and want to know where it stands, written from outside the description rather than copied out of it: 'status', 'where are we', 'give me an update', 'what has been finished since yesterday', 'is anything stuck'. The near-misses borrow real vocabulary from the neighbouring skills so the contrast is not zero: a request for a decision (hsi-operator), a request to save state before a window closes (context-steward), a request to judge a repo (repo-triage) and a request to draw how a system works (system-map). 'what needs me' and 'what is waiting on me' are deliberately NOT here as positives: hsi-operator owns them, and writing them as positives for this skill would make two skills claim the same sentence. If a positive fails, fix the description, not the case.

cases.prompt: status report on the work so far
where are we on everything, give me a quick status
give me an update on what the agents have been doing
what got finished since yesterday and is there proof
is anything stalled or blocked, and for how long
how far along is each objective, and what is the finish line for it
what should I decide about the retry limit
save the status of this session before the window closes
is this repo any good, should we adopt it as a dependency
draw an architecture diagram of the workflow between our repos
